## Grammarly boosts subscription revenue 29% and ROAS 23% with AI-powered search

Grammarly sought to accelerate its global lifetime value of users while improving efficiency. They focused on AI-powered search and implemented the following:  

1.  **Modernized measurement** by importing lifetime values and using them for value-based bidding to optimize for their highest-value users
2.  **Consolidated keywords and used broad match** to capture new queries and increase search coverage

Open a new Google Ads account for a store and Google will steer you toward Performance Max within a few clicks. Its help pages call it the best way to maximize online sales, and for a large store with years of order data, it often is.

A new store doesn't have years of order data. It has a product feed, a purchase tag that was tested last week, and a budget that can't afford to teach an algorithm from scratch. For that store, the first Shopping campaign should be the one where you can still see what's happening and set every bid yourself: Standard Shopping on manual bids.

*   [Report this post](https://www.linkedin.com/uas/login?session_redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.linkedin.com%2Fposts%2Fryanjenkins88_im-seen-plenty-of-competitor-bid-strategies-activity-7364556733727379456-KhDP&trk=public_post_ellipsis-menu-semaphore-sign-in-redirect&guestReportContentType=POST&_f=guest-reporting)

I'm seen plenty of competitor bid strategies, but this has to take the cake. 😂😂 I even thought that I clicked on the wrong link when I got the site and I realised I was on JD Sports.. By the way this is a breach of Google policy so don't try it. Here's why: 1. Trademark Misuse JD Sports is using “Footlocker” in the ad headline. Foot Locker is a competitor and a registered trademark. Google Ads policies prohibit advertisers from using a competitor’s trademark in a misleading way — particularly in headlines, ad text, or display URLs — unless they are an authorised reseller, informative site, or the trademark owner. 2. Misleading Content The ad makes it appear as though JD Sports is Foot Locker or affiliated with them. This creates consumer confusion and could be seen as “passing off,” where one brand tries to capture traffic meant for another. 3. Policy Coverage Under Google Ads’ Trademarks Policy, advertisers generally cannot use third-party trademarks in ad copy if it misleads users about the advertiser’s relationship with the trademark owner. Exceptions apply if the advertiser is: An authorised reseller of genuine products from that brand, or Using the term descriptively (not as branding). In this case, the headline “Footlocker” is not descriptive — it looks like branding.
